item.title: Clinical Patterns
item.description:
Everything can have or be a clinical pattern. It could be the pattern of someone sitting crossed-legged way too long every day. It could also be the pattern of a skin lesion in a specific part of the body. Which patterns are useful? Those that are common. Those that inform treatment well. Those that correspond well to a certain prognosis or even to a diagnosis.

If we are talking structures, we could have a specific pattern for every nerve, muscles, tendon, ligament, bone. But this only makes sense if we can go one step back and identify clinical patterns for any of these structures in general, not one specifically. And then a way of deducing the specific structure, e.g. through palpation and anatomical knowledge in addition to the general features.

item.title: Forms and Fighting
item.description: Fixed movement patterns, forms, are central to any martial art. You want to get better at a certain way of moving, so you focus on a movement and try to work the desired quality in isolation. If a boxer wants to get better at hitting hard, he practises his punches in isolation. Or he might practise his footwork. Forms can also be practised with a partner, maybe pad combinations involving ducking and weaving. In traditional martial arts, forms might even be at the center of the training, involving complex patterns stringed together into long sequences.

item.title: About
item.description: Reflections of someone slow and scatter-brained stumbling through the world of people, things and ideas.

item.title: Feeling Dumb
item.description:
It is always a marvel to look at someone who just gets something: Who just looks at a problem and sees the solution. Who effortlessly replicates a move that was only shown once or applies a technique in sparring directly after learning it. And it is very easy to feel dumb in comparison, struggling to achieve the same thing with full effort and still falling short.

It is frustrating, exhausting, degrading. It is also lovely. There is so much potential in these moments and so much power in the simple step of deciding to stay with them instead of copping out. And in the decision to return to the same situation a few times.
